plan_summary.objective: Fix run-artifact drift by aligning runtime and agent artifact paths, repairing three historical runs into history/<run-id>/ directories, and removing the lingering one-time migration helper.
plan_summary.approach: Treat active/<run_id>/ and history/<run_id>/ as the only supported runtime-owned run locations, add failing-first workflow tests for sibling artifact drift and flat-history repair, simplify finalization around one reconciliation path, then repair the three named runs with an idempotent tested mechanism.
key_steps: Add failing behavior tests that reproduce orphaned sibling artifact trees and flat history JSON repair gaps.
Refactor workflow finalization/reconciliation logic, remove _migrate_legacy_artifacts, and keep live/template workflow.py in sync.
Update agent prompt path contracts and wrapper tests so they stop encoding unsupported .ai/workflows/runs/<run_id>/... paths.
Repair the three named historical runs by creating/normalizing history directories and moving plans/handoffs/logs under them.
Run focused workflow/contract verification plus full regression and template drift checks.
focused_tests: python3 -m pytest tests/test_workflow.py -k colocates_sibling_run_artifacts or sibling_artifact_tree or flat_history_json_to_directory -v
root_cause_hypotheses: Runtime path change landed without updating agent prompts/examples and contract tests, so workers still targeted sibling .ai/workflows/runs/<run_id>/... directories.
Workflow tests only proved moves when artifacts were already inside active/<run_id>/.
Review relied on green tests and did not inspect archived filesystem state.
Finish/runtime semantics allowed done because no exit criterion asserts artifact colocation.
_migrate_legacy_artifacts handled a different legacy layout and never covered sibling per-run directories or plans.
